Should You Use a HELOC for an Emergency? What Homeowners Should Know

Unlike an emergency fund, which consists of money already saved, a HELOC is borrowed money that must be repaid with interest. It may serve as a backup source of funds for some homeowners, but it should not be treated as a direct replacement for emergency savings.
  • Written By: Phroogal Staff
  • Last Updated: July 30, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 40:21
Instaread

Disclosure: The article may contain affiliate links from partners who may compensate us. However, the words, opinions, and reviews are our own. Learn how we make money to support our mission.

This article is sponsored by Members 1st Federal Credit Union.

When an unexpected home repair, medical bill, or other major expense arises, homeowners may wonder where to turn for money. A home equity line of credit, or HELOC, can provide access to a substantial credit line, often at a lower interest rate than a credit card. But it also carries serious risks because the debt is secured by the borrower’s home.

Unlike an emergency fund, which consists of money already saved, a HELOC is borrowed money that must be repaid with interest. It may serve as a backup source of funds for some homeowners, but it should not be treated as a direct replacement for emergency savings.

What Is a Home Equity Line of Credit?

A HELOC is a revolving line of credit secured by the borrower’s home. Like a credit card, it allows the borrower to access money up to an approved limit, repay what was borrowed, and potentially borrow again.

According to Bankrate’s 2026 Annual Emergency Savings Report, 47% of Americans said they had enough available savings, income, or access to funds to cover a $1,000 emergency expense. Only 30% said they would pay the expense directly from savings. For a homeowner facing a major HVAC replacement, medical bill, or urgent repair, finding several thousand dollars can become a serious financial challenge. That’s why many homeowners wonder whether using a home equity line of credit for emergencies makes financial sense.

The Advantages of Using a Home Equity Line of Credit for Emergencies

A HELOC offers several practical benefits for emergency situations.

Access to a Potentially Large Credit Line

Because a HELOC is secured by home equity, it may offer a larger borrowing limit than unsecured options such as credit cards or personal loans. For example, a homeowner with a property valued at $300,000 and a remaining mortgage balance of $200,000 has $100,000 in equity.

However, that does not mean the homeowner can borrow the full $100,000. The approved credit line will depend on factors such as the lender’s requirements, the homeowner’s income and creditworthiness, the existing mortgage balance, and the lender’s maximum combined loan-to-value ratio. Some products allow qualified borrowers to access a high percentage of their available equity, but borrowing limits vary.

Lower Interest Rates Than Credit Cards

In May 2026, the average interest rate on credit card accounts that were assessed interest was 22.15%, according to Federal Reserve data. HELOC rates are often lower than credit card rates, although the rate offered will depend on the lender, market conditions, and the borrower’s qualifications.

Flexible Repayment Options

During the draw period, many HELOCs require only interest payments on the amount actually borrowed. If someone borrows $10,000 to repair a burst pipe that flooded their basement, they pay interest only on that $10,000 while they rebuild their finances.

Keep in mind that interest-only payments can provide short-term flexibility, but they do not reduce the amount borrowed. When the draw period ends and repayment begins, monthly payments may increase because the borrower must begin repaying both principal and interest.

The Significant Risks of Relying on Home Equity

The risks are substantial and deserve serious consideration.

Your Home Is Used as Collateral

Turning an emergency expense into debt secured by a home raises the stakes considerably. If the borrower cannot meet the loan terms, the home may be at risk. The lender may have the legal right to foreclosure of the property.

Your Credit Line Can Be Frozen or Reduced

A HELOC is not guaranteed to remain fully available. A lender may reduce or freeze access to additional borrowing if the home’s value declines substantially or the borrower’s financial circumstances change. That means a HELOC may become less dependable during the same economic conditions that create a need for emergency funds.

Variable Interest Rates Can Increase Costs

Many HELOCs carry variable interest rates tied to market conditions. Monthly payments can climb if rates rise, adding financial pressure during an already difficult time.

Upfront Costs and Fees

Depending on the lender and product, opening or maintaining a HELOC may involve appraisal fees, closing costs, annual fees, early-closure fees, or other charges. Homeowners should review the loan estimate and product disclosures before deciding whether the line is worth opening.

Is a HELOC Better Than Keeping Cash Savings?

For many homeowners, the decision is not necessarily cash savings or a HELOC. A HELOC may function as a secondary backup for expenses that exceed available savings, provided the homeowner understands the costs and has a realistic repayment plan.

A HELOC Option From Members 1st Federal Credit Union

Members 1st Federal Credit Union offers a Home Equity Freedom Line of Credit that allows qualified homeowners to borrow against available home equity up to 100%. The product currently includes an introductory annual percentage rate for the first six months, followed by a variable rate. Members may also have the option to convert all or part of an outstanding balance to a fixed-rate term.

The line includes a 10-year draw period and may allow interest-only payments during that period. Because interest-only payments do not reduce principal, borrowers should understand how their payments may change when the repayment period begins. Eligibility, rates, borrowing limits, property requirements, fees, and approval timing depend on the applicant and the credit union’s current terms.

Homeowners considering the product should review the complete disclosures and compare the rate, fees, repayment structure, and risks with other available options before borrowing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are answers to common questions about using a HELOC for emergency purposes.

  1. When should someone apply for a HELOC?

    A HELOC is usually more useful when it has been opened before an emergency occurs. Applying after a crisis begins may not provide money quickly enough, and approval is not guaranteed.

  2. Is a HELOC good for unexpected expenses?

    A HELOC may be an option for a large, necessary expense that exceeds available savings, particularly when the homeowner already has an open line and a reliable repayment plan. It is generally less appropriate for routine spending or expenses that could be handled without placing the home at risk.

  3. When should someone not use a HELOC for an emergency?

    A HELOC may not be appropriate when income is unstable, future payments would be difficult to manage, the expense is not essential, or the homeowner would need to borrow repeatedly without a repayment plan. Homeowners should also consider how a higher variable rate or lower property value could affect their finances.

  4. Is it better to use cash savings or a HELOC for an emergency?

    Cash savings are generally less risky because they do not create debt or place the home at risk. A HELOC may provide a secondary option for a large expense that exceeds available savings, but the homeowner should compare it with alternatives and understand the repayment terms before borrowing.

  5. Deciding on Your Financial Safety Net

    A HELOC can provide homeowners with financial flexibility, but that flexibility comes with real costs and risks. It is borrowed money, not emergency savings, and the borrower’s home secures the debt.
    Before using a HELOC, consider the urgency of the expense, how much cash is already available, the total cost of borrowing, and whether the payments would remain manageable if income changed or interest rates increased. For some homeowners, a HELOC may be a useful secondary safety net. It should complement—not replace—the work of building accessible cash savings over time.

Data preferences

Manage your data

You can choose how your personal data is used. Vendors want your permission to do the following:

Purposes

Store and/or access information on a device

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.

View details

Use limited data to select advertising

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times an ad is presented to you).

View details

Create profiles for personalised advertising

Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

View details

Use profiles to select personalised advertising

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on your advertising profiles, which can reflect your activity on this service or other websites or apps (like the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects.

View details

Create profiles to personalise content

Information about your activity on this service (for instance, forms you submit, non-advertising content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (such as your previous activity on this service or other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (which might for example include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present content that appears more relevant based on your possible interests, such as by adapting the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find content that matches your interests.

View details

Use profiles to select personalised content

Content presented to you on this service can be based on your content personalisation profiles, which can reflect your activity on this or other services (for instance, the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects. This can for example be used to adapt the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find (non-advertising) content that matches your interests.

View details

Measure advertising performance

Information regarding which advertising is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine how well an advert has worked for you or other users and whether the goals of the advertising were reached. For instance, whether you saw an ad, whether you clicked on it, whether it led you to buy a product or visit a website, etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of advertising campaigns.

View details

Measure content performance

Information regarding which content is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine whether the (non-advertising) content e.g. reached its intended audience and matched your interests. For instance, whether you read an article, watch a video, listen to a podcast or look at a product description, how long you spent on this service and the web pages you visit etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of (non-advertising) content that is shown to you.

View details

Understand audiences through statistics or combinations of data from different sources

Reports can be generated based on the combination of data sets (like user profiles, statistics, market research, analytics data) regarding your interactions and those of other users with advertising or (non-advertising) content to identify common characteristics (for instance, to determine which target audiences are more receptive to an ad campaign or to certain contents).

View details

Develop and improve services

Information about your activity on this service, such as your interaction with ads or content, can be very helpful to improve products and services and to build new products and services based on user interactions, the type of audience, etc. This specific purpose does not include the development or improvement of user profiles and identifiers.

View details

Use limited data to select content

Content presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type, or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times a video or an article is presented to you).

View details

Special purposes

Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors

Your data can be used to monitor for and prevent unusual and possibly fraudulent activity (for example, regarding advertising, ad clicks by bots), and ensure systems and processes work properly and securely. It can also be used to correct any problems you, the publisher or the advertiser may encounter in the delivery of content and ads and in your interaction with them.

View details

Deliver and present advertising and content

Certain information (like an IP address or device capabilities) is used to ensure the technical compatibility of the content or advertising, and to facilitate the transmission of the content or ad to your device.

View details

Save and communicate privacy choices

The choices you make regarding the purposes and entities listed in this notice are saved and made available to those entities in the form of digital signals (such as a string of characters). This is necessary in order to enable both this service and those entities to respect such choices.

View details

Features

These means of processing can be used solely in pursuit of one or several purposes for which you are given a choice in this notice.

Match and combine data from other data sources

Information about your activity on this service may be matched and combined with other information relating to you and originating from various sources (for instance your activity on a separate online service, your use of a loyalty card in-store, or your answers to a survey), in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

View details

Link different devices

In support of the purposes explained in this notice, your device might be considered as likely linked to other devices that belong to you or your household (for instance because you are logged in to the same service on both your phone and your computer, or because you may use the same Internet connection on both devices).

View details

Identify devices based on information transmitted automatically

Your device might be distinguished from other devices based on information it automatically sends when accessing the Internet (for instance, the IP address of your Internet connection or the type of browser you are using) in support of the purposes exposed in this notice.

View details

Special features

Use precise geolocation data

With your acceptance, your precise location (within a radius of less than 500 metres) may be used in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.

  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
